text: There was a smell of fresh carpet and over done coffee. It was our first day. We were 6 people sitting around the table, which was very glossy. Our name tents were in front of us, like little white sails. The HR director welcomed us and smiled, very calibrated. Then we went through the slides. Mission, vision, values, where to park, how to log in. Our badges were all lined up in a row. The photos were already outdated, because we were so nervous. The welcome kit was there, with a mug, a lanyard, like the colour of unripe fruit. And we introduced ourselves, said our names, where we were from, what we did before. Voices went up and down, like the tide. Someone laughed really loud at a joke about IT passwords. Someone wrote everything down in a notebook, like the future would come and take it. The scratching of the pen was really soft. In the afternoon we went through the modules. Harassment, security, expense reports. We had our laptops open, clicking through. The screens were glowing, very pale and patient. The trainer was talking, his voice was like a ceiling fan, very steady and forgettable. I found out where the good coffee was, how to reserve a room, the shortcut that saves me four minutes. Small maps, already filling. At 5 pm we went our separate ways, like leaves falling off a curb. I stood at the window and watched the parking lot empty. The building was behind me, and it was full of lights. A thousand small lights, each one a person I didn’t know yet. My badge was warm from my hand. Tomorrow, I thought. And it felt like less a door, more like a lamp that was left on.
